content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In mainstream Christian teaching, 'seed' most commonly symbolizes the Word of God — the gospel message sown into human hearts, which germinates and bears spiritual fruit depending on the condition of the hearer. This meaning is treated as authoritative because Jesus himself supplies the interpretation within the parable of the sower ('the seed is the word of God').","primary_basis":["Luke 8:11 ('The seed is the word of God')","Matthew 13:3-23 (parable of the sower and Jesus' explanation)","Mark 4:3-20, 26-32 (parable of the sower; the growing seed; the mustard seed)","1 Peter 1:23 (born again 'of incorruptible seed, by the word of God')","Isaiah 55:10-11 (God's word compared to seed/rain that accomplishes its purpose)","James 1:21 (the 'implanted word' able to save souls)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Seed as offspring/descendants, culminating in Christ: the 'seed of the woman' who crushes the serpent (the protoevangelium) and the 'seed of Abraham' through whom all nations are blessed, which Paul identifies as Christ. In much theological and messianic exegesis this is the central symbolic thread of the whole Bible.","basis":["Genesis 3:15","Genesis 12:7; 13:15; 22:17-18","Galatians 3:16, 29","2 Samuel 7:12","Romans 9:7-8"],"prominence":"dominant"},{"meaning":"Seed as a symbol of death and resurrection: a seed must fall into the ground and die to bear fruit, used of Christ's death and of the resurrection body.","basis":["John 12:24","1 Corinthians 15:36-44"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Seed as the principle of sowing and reaping — moral/spiritual consequence: one reaps what one sows, whether to the flesh or the Spirit; also generosity and its harvest.","basis":["Galatians 6:7-8","2 Corinthians 9:6-10","Hosea 10:12","Psalm 126:5-6"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Seed as the divine nature or principle of regeneration abiding in the believer ('God's seed abides in him'), sometimes read as the Holy Spirit or the new birth.","basis":["1 John 3:9","1 Peter 1:23"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Seed as faith itself, even in the smallest quantity ('faith as a grain of mustard seed'), or as the small beginnings of the kingdom of God that grows into something great.","basis":["Matthew 17:20","Matthew 13:31-32","Luke 17:6"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"In prosperity-gospel or 'seed-faith' teaching, seed as money or offerings given to a ministry in expectation of a multiplied financial return.","basis":["2 Corinthians 9:6-10 (as commonly appropriated)","Luke 6:38 (as commonly appropriated)"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"'Seed' is one of the richest and most multivalent biblical symbols, and interpreters recognize several legitimate strands rather than a single exclusive meaning. Two strands compete for primacy: (1) seed = the Word of God/gospel, which has the strongest claim to a 'consensus symbolic meaning' because Scripture itself defines it that way (Luke 8:11), and (2) seed = offspring culminating in Christ (Gen 3:15; Gal 3:16), which is arguably the more theologically central usage across the canon and is dominant in biblical-theological and messianic readings. Which is called 'primary' depends on whether one is asking about symbolic usage in parables and devotional teaching (Word of God) or the redemptive-historical storyline (Christ as promised seed). Both are so widely recognized that either could reasonably be listed first; the remaining meanings (death/resurrection, sowing-reaping, regeneration, faith/kingdom growth) are well attested but secondary."}
